info.bio:
Abel Makkonen Tesfaye, mejor conocido por su nombre artístico The Weeknd (Toronto, Canadá, 16 de febrero de 1990), es un cantante, compositor y productor canadiense.

A finales de 2010, Tesfaye subió anónimamente varias canciones a YouTube bajo el nombre "The Weeknd". Lanzó tres mixtapes de nueve pistas a lo largo de 2011: House of Balloons, Thursday and Echoes of Silence, que eran muy aclamadas. Al año siguiente, lanzo su álbum recopilatorio

podcast.title: Post-2000 International Impact
podcast.body: Since 2000, The Weeknd has contributed to Canada's "international coolness factor," demonstrating the country's continued ability to produce artists who achieve global recognition beyond traditional record sales metrics. He represents a new wave of Canadian superstars on the world stage. "since 2000 the country has continued to punch far, far above its weight in the world stage, with artists like Justin Bieber, the weekend, Drake and Arcade Fire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Roots of the 90s CanRock Explosion

podcast.title: Sixth Highest Earner (2016)
podcast.body: The Weeknd secured the sixth position on the Forbes list, earning approximately 90 million dollars. He has consistently climbed this list year after year. A significant portion of his income was generated from over 100 concerts performed during the year, alongside an album launch (likely "Starboy"). His income from streaming is also significantly increasing. "ha tenido más de 100 conciertos durante este año y es prácticamente en lo que se ha basado todo su ingreso."

srcs.episode: Los artistas que más dinero han ganado este año y por qué.

podcast.title: Extended Chart Longevity (2020-2021)
podcast.body: "Blinding Lights" achieved remarkable chart longevity, spending a record 90 weeks on the Hot 100. This allowed it to be the number one song of 2020 and the number three song of 2021. Although its record for total weeks on the Hot 100 was surpassed by Glass Animals' "Heat Waves," it still holds the records for most time spent in the Top 5 (43 weeks) and Top 10 (57 weeks). "In total, blinding lights spent a record 90 weeks on the hot 100."

podcast.title: AI Voice Cloning in "Heart on My Sleeve" (2023)
podcast.body: A "fake" version of The Weeknd's voice was featured in an AI-generated fake duet with Drake, created by Ghostwriter and released in April 2023. The track, titled "Heart on My Sleeve," ignited immediate and intense debates regarding the ethics and legality of using an artist's voice and likeness without their explicit consent. "The one that got everybody's attention was a fake duet between a fake Drake and a fake the weekend created and posted in April 2023 by someone named Ghost Rider."

podcast.title: All Album Tracks Charting
podcast.body: In December 2016, all 18 tracks from The Weeknd's album "Starboy" placed on the Hot 100, including the title track (#1) and deep cuts like "Die for You" (#43). This "charts stunt" was a phenomenon made possible by digital music, signaling a "higher gear" in his imperial phase and burnishing his imperiality. "In December of 2016, all 18 tracks from the album placed on the Hot 100."

podcast.title: Canadian Export Success
podcast.body: The Weeknd is cited as one of the contemporary artists responsible for the increasing global export of Canadian music. "thanks to stars like Drake and the weekend, Justin Bieber, Alessia Cara, and a long list of artists that came before."

podcast.title: Dominance of Streaming Medium
podcast.body: The Weeknd is an example of an artist whose music heavily dominates the streaming medium, particularly within pop, R&B, and hip-hop genres. "You know, Drake, Ed Sheeran, the weekend, Justin Bieber."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Trying to be a Superstar in the 21st Century

podcast.title: Early Mystery & Permanent Hitmaker Status
podcast.body: In the early 2010s, The Weeknd (Abel Tesfaye) began recording with a shrouded identity and left-of-center music, drawing comparisons to early David Bowie. However, unlike Bowie, once he started scoring big pop hits, he became a "permanent hitmaker" and a pop force, never returning to his initial left-of-center approach. "Listeners may recall that when Abel Tessfe, the singer known as The Weekend, began recording in the early 2010s, his identity was shrouded in mystery, and his music was considered very left of center, not unlike early Bowie."

podcast.title: Influence from Daft Punk's Discovery
podcast.body: The Weeknd, along with Drake, is among the contemporary artists whose music builds upon foundational elements introduced by Daft Punk's "Discovery" album, such as potent disco passages, vocoders, and saturated autotune, which were initially criticized. "Hoy es una de las bases de música, es como de Wikendo o Drake."

srcs.episode: Daft Punk - Interstella 5555

podcast.title: Replaced Self at #1
podcast.body: In the fall of 2015, The Weeknd (Able Tesfaye) replaced his number one hit "Can't Feel My Face" with his own "The Hills," a feat that immediately qualified him for imperial status. "Able Tessfe, aka The Weekend, joined the very exclusive club of artists I mentioned earlier who replaced themselves at number one on the Hot 100."

podcast.title: Streaming Success and New Content Strategy
podcast.body: The Weeknd is rapidly increasing his income from streaming and is expected to enter and remain in the top three. This is attributed to his adoption of a new content publication system that aligns with the listening habits of young audiences, who prioritize novelty in musical material rather than just a large volume of it. "están adoptando un nuevo sistema de publicación de contenido que se está adaptando a los nuevos sistemas de escucha que tiene la gente joven, que no demandan tanto material musical sino novedades de material musical."

podcast.title: YouTube Discovery and Signing (Capital Music Group)
podcast.body: The Weeknd was first discovered on YouTube. Nate Albert, an A&R executive, was instrumental in finding him and subsequently fending off more than two dozen competing offers to sign him to Capital Music Group. "The Weekend... they were all first found on YouTube."

xref.title: A&R Superstar
xref.body: Nate Albert is recognized as a "superstar of A&R" for his pivotal role in discovering The Weeknd. He successfully secured The Weeknd's signing to Capital Music Group despite more than two dozen competing offers from other labels. "Take Nate Albert. He was the one who found the weekend and then fended off more than two dozen competing offers to sign up to Capital Music Group."
